belief: God values me for what I accomplish.
origins: Children who are praised mostly for grades, achievements, or helpfulness often conclude that love is earned. In adulthood this becomes a quiet belief: God is pleased when I produce and disappointed when I do not. Church can reinforce it when service is applauded more than simple presence.
teaches: Paul writes, “For it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God, not by works, so that no one can boast.” “He saved us, not by the righteous deeds we had done, but according to His mercy.” “God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” When the disciples rejoiced in their success, Jesus said, “rejoice that your names are written in heaven.” Zephaniah says the LORD “will rejoice over you with gladness; He will quiet you with His love.” God’s delight in us is not a wage.
self_statements: God is pleased only when I achieve.
I have to earn His approval.
When I fail, He is disappointed.
My worth goes up and down with my results.
I am loved for what I do.
errors: Feeling worthless when I fail and concluding God sees me that way.
Believing I am either accomplished and loved, or failing and unloved.
Insisting that I must earn God’s love.
Assuming God is disappointed in me.
questions: When was I praised for what I did rather than who I was?
What does “not by works” tell me about how God sees me?
Did Christ die for me when I was productive or when I was a sinner?
What does Zephaniah say God does over me?
How would my days look different if I believed I was already loved?
What would I do from love instead of for approval?
truth: God values me because I am His, not because of what I accomplish. His love was given while I was still a sinner. I can work and serve from love, not for approval.
hw_truths: I am saved by grace, not works.
God proved His love while I was a sinner.
My name is written in heaven.
He rejoices over me with singing.
My worth does not rise and fall with results.
log: Each morning, say “I am loved before I do anything today,” and note one task done from love.
actions: Write who taught you that love is earned.
Imagine God singing over you, not tallying your day.
Write one sentence that distinguishes who you are from what you do.
Do one thing for no reward.
prayer: Father, thank You for loving me before I did anything. Free me from trying to earn what You have already given. Help me work and serve from love, resting in Your delight in me. Amen.
hw_questions: When was I praised for what I did?
What does “not by works” mean for me?
How does God feel about me on a bad day?
What would I do from love?
What can I do quietly for no reward?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I am saved by grace, not by works, so God’s love does not depend on what I accomplish.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “God values me for what I accomplish.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
